sample.rationale: Both refuse to smooth over damage/loss — Whisper marks what it couldn't hear instead of guessing; the butterfly joint marks where the wood broke instead of hiding it. Each treats the visible seam as more honest than a polished, seamless result.
sample.evidence: "I refuse to invent words I didn't hear. If a section is unintelligible, I mark it [unintelligible] rather than guess... the diff at each step becomes an honest measure of what narration loses." || "Nakashima didn't hide the crack. He cut a bowtie-shaped inlay across it... proof of the repair, not a cover for it."

sample.source: Move the Ink, Don't Redraw It
sample.rationale: Both independently arrived at the same law: a fixed, unregenerated structure is the precondition for subtle variation to be legible — remake the structure each pass (redraw, re-rule) and the signal (the drift, the hand) dissolves into noise/boil rather than becoming visible.
sample.evidence: "the procedural paper tooth is generated once and reused on every frame. A static substrate cannot boil... at every layer where stability matters, fix the thing once, don't remake it each step" || "A hand-ruled line is never perfectly straight; draw the same grid a thousand times and no two lines fall the same... The grid holds still so the drift can be seen; take it away and the difference vanishes into noise."

sample.rationale: Both entries make the identical rhetorical move of explicitly rejecting representation in favor of literal identity — the interface IS the physics; the virtue IS the nature — refusing to let a faithful expression be demoted to a stand-in for the real thing.
sample.evidence: "what you see is not a visualization bolted onto the sound, it is the same delay-line state that produces the sound, drawn in space... The waveguide's spatial state is exact, not a metaphor." || "This is not metaphor. It is operational principle... The virtue and the nature are not separate."
